data.note:
Note: Specimen s_9b92bf868e was camptothecin (PubChem CID 24360, ChEMBL CHEMBL65, e22; BBBC021 structure agrees). BBBC021 annotates as DNA replication; ChEMBL has no curated mechanism (e22).

My final call Eg5 inhibitors (p0.42) was wrong. Camptothecin is a topoisomerase I inhibitor causing replication fork collision and S-phase DNA damage: reviewed in Pommier Nat Rev Cancer 2006 PMID 16990856 and Pourquier & Pommier Adv Cancer Res 2001 PMID 11034544.

Why I failed: Low-dose (0.03 µM) showed nuc_area z+28, large irregular/polyploid nuclei - e3/e11 called Aurora-like, but per-well atlas on that well alone (e19) was 8/10 DNA damage (chlorambucil, mitomycin C, cisplatin, etoposide), not Aurora/Eg5. I discounted it because tub_mean was normal and pooled atlas e6 mixed doses. At high doses (1-10 µM) co-extreme act_std z+69, tub_mean z+28, tub_glcm z+32, nuc small z-24, frac_mitotic_like z+14-18, roundness, cell loss mimicked Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest. Per-well high-dose atlas e17 was Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 2/10 vs Microtubule destabilizers 2/10, overlapping similarities 0.83-0.87. Microscopist e10 called high-dose "unknown, not actin-only" with condensed nuclei and actin/tubulin collapse - consistent with apoptosis secondary to DNA damage, not primary Eg5 or actin. I should have weighted dose progression: DNA replication stress → G2 arrest/large nuclei at low dose → apoptosis/mitotic-like condensation at high dose, rather than averaging phenotypes. Lesson: biphasic large→small nuclei + increasing cell loss + modest DNA integrated increase is classic DNA damage/replication, even when cytoskeletal z-scores are numerically larger due to cell rounding/shrinkage artifacts.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth is camptothecin - DNA replication / Topoisomerase I - mediated DNA damage - PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, PMID 8305535. Agent final call was Eg5 inhibitors p=0.42 (first call Actin disruptors p=0.55). Incorrect.

What evidence got right: The dose-series captured a real biphasic nuclear phenotype that is consistent retrospectively with replication stress. Low-mid dose w_1ec2bbb0a5 (0.03 uM): nuc_area z=+28.0, cell_area +12.6, cell_major_axis +13.6 (e3) with microscopist "density similar, Aurora-like" 6 observations (e11) and dose_response nuc_area rho=-0.80 (e7). High dose w_f6df577edc (10 uM): nuc_area becomes -24.4 at 1 uM (e4), nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 (e2) and dose_response nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0 (e13), frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0 (e8), tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9), act_std z=+69.0, act_glcm_contrast +33.7 (e2). That large-to-small/irregular transition plus increasing mitotic-like fraction does occur with camptothecin: low-dose S-phase arrest/enlarged nuclei progressing to condensed/fragmented nuclei and secondary cytoskeletal collapse at high dose. The review correctly flagged that high-dose actin and tubulin deviations were co-extreme: act_std +69 but tub_glcm_contrast +29.5 (e4), tub mean high, act_glcm +27.3, tub_glcm +23.2 at 0.3 uM (e5) - equally consistent with Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest as actin-only, with roundness and high frac_mitotic_like z=+18, and microscopist high-dose call "unknown, not actin-only" (e10).

What misled and why missed: I over-weighted extreme actin/tubulin texture as primary MoA. act_std z=+69 at 65 cells (e2) and act_std rho=+0.80 (e12) anchored Actin disruptors hypothesis 0.50 (e15), then Eg5 0.42 after per-well high-dose atlas Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 2/10 vs Destabilizers 2/10 (e17). Pooled atlas Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 3/10 vs Cholesterol 2/10 (e6) mixed biphasic doses and gave overlapping similarities 0.80-0.88, which I treated as discriminative. Dose_response n=4 gives unstable rho (p=0.2 for nuc_area and act_std) but I used the directionality as strong. I prematurely pruned DNA damage/DNA replication: hypothesis 0.02 and 0.005 at step 15 despite e3/e11 large-nuclei signal, and absent at step 18. This was an acquisition/interpretation choice: I sampled 4 wells across doses (e2-e5) which was good to see the switch, but then compared pooled wells to atlas and focused microscopy on mitotic vs actin, not DNA damage markers. DNA replication inhibitors can produce secondary high tub_mean and frac_mitotic-like signals due to G2/M checkpoint arrest and apoptotic condensation, which I read as Eg5/Aurora-specific.

The critical missed evidence was within the run: per-well low-dose atlas e19 returned DNA damage 8/10, DNA replication 1/10 after I had already submitted Eg5. That was the only comparison isolating the 0.03 uM large-nucleus phenotype (e3) from the high-dose collapsed phenotype, and it strongly supported truth. I included e19 in the second conclusion's key_evidence but did not update probabilities to favor DNA damage/replication, retaining Eg5 because high-dose per-well e17 still favored Eg5. In hindsight, ChEMBL lookup returning "mechanisms: none curated" (e21/e22) and name/structure agreement gave no prior to rescue, so atlas needed careful per-dose interpretation. A DNA damage follow-up (gammaH2AX, pH3-Ser10 FACS for polyploidy vs mitotic arrest, DNA content) as suggested in rationale would have been more diagnostic than phalloidin vs tubulin alone, and would distinguish replication stress large nuclei from Aurora/Eg5 polyploidy/mono-polar mitosis.

Lesson: for camptothecin-like agents PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, biphasic nuclear size with decreasing form factor and modest cell_count loss (rho -0.60 p0.4, e14) plus extreme late actin/tubulin texture should prompt DNA damage/replication hypothesis even when tubulin/mitotic metrics rise.
what_was_right: Detected biphasic nuc_area +28 at 0.03 uM (e3) to -24.4 at 1 uM (e4) with rho -0.80 (e7) and rho -1.00 for form factor (e13) - true for replication stress
Flagged co-extreme actin (z+69 e2) and tubulin (z+29.5 e4, +23.2 e5) with high frac_mitotic_like rho+1.00 (e8) as ambiguous mitotic vs cytoskeletal
Review correctly noted pooled atlas e6 Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 3/10 overlapping similarities 0.80-0.88 not clean
what_was_wrong: Over-weighted act_std z+69.0 and act_glcm +33.7 (e2) for Actin disruptors then Eg5 4/10 (e17)
Pruned DNA damage 0.02 and DNA replication 0.005 at step15 to 0 by step18 despite e3 large nuclei and e11 Aurora-like visual
Interpreted tub_mean rho+1.00 (e9) and frac_mitotic_like rho+1.00 (e8) as specific for Eg5/Aurora not secondary to DNA damage checkpoint/apoptosis
Ignored per-well low-dose atlas e19 DNA damage 8/10 / replication 1/10 that directly supported truth after second submit

Unblinded truth is camptothecin - DNA replication / Topoisomerase I - mediated DNA damage - PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, PMID 8305535. Agent final call was Eg5 inhibitors p=0.42 (first call Actin disruptors p=0.55). Incorrect.

What evidence got right: The dose-series captured a real biphasic nuclear phenotype that is consistent retrospectively with replication stress. Low-mid dose w_1ec2bbb0a5 (0.03 uM): nuc_area z=+28.0, cell_area +12.6, cell_major_axis +13.6 (e3) with microscopist "density similar, Aurora-like" 6 observations (e11) and dose_response nuc_area rho=-0.80 (e7). High dose w_f6df577edc (10 uM): nuc_area becomes -24.4 at 1 uM (e4), nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 (e2) and dose_response nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0 (e13), frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0 (e8), tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9), act_std z=+69.0, act_glcm_contrast +33.7 (e2). That large-to-small/irregular transition plus increasing mitotic-like fraction does occur with camptothecin: low-dose S-phase arrest/enlarged nuclei progressing to condensed/fragmented nuclei and secondary cytoskeletal collapse at high dose. The review correctly flagged that high-dose actin and tubulin deviations were co-extreme: act_std +69 but tub_glcm_contrast +29.5 (e4), tub mean high, act_glcm +27.3, tub_glcm +23.2 at 0.3 uM (e5) - equally consistent with Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest as actin-only, with roundness and high frac_mitotic_like z=+18, and microscopist high-dose call "unknown, not actin-only" (e10).

What misled and why missed: I over-weighted extreme actin/tubulin texture as primary MoA. act_std z=+69 at 65 cells (e2) and act_std rho=+0.80 (e12) anchored Actin disruptors hypothesis 0.50 (e15), then Eg5 0.42 after per-well high-dose atlas Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 2/10 vs Destabilizers 2/10 (e17). Pooled atlas Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 3/10 vs Cholesterol 2/10 (e6) mixed biphasic doses and gave overlapping similarities 0.80-0.88, which I treated as discriminative. Dose_response n=4 gives unstable rho (p=0.2 for nuc_area and act_std) but I used the directionality as strong. I prematurely pruned DNA damage/DNA replication: hypothesis 0.02 and 0.005 at step 15 despite e3/e11 large-nuclei signal, and absent at step 18. This was an acquisition/interpretation choice: I sampled 4 wells across doses (e2-e5) which was good to see the switch, but then compared pooled wells to atlas and focused microscopy on mitotic vs actin, not DNA damage markers. DNA replication inhibitors can produce secondary high tub_mean and frac_mitotic-like signals due to G2/M checkpoint arrest and apoptotic condensation, which I read as Eg5/Aurora-specific.

The critical missed evidence was within the run: per-well low-dose atlas e19 returned DNA damage 8/10, DNA replication 1/10 after I had already submitted Eg5. That was the only comparison isolating the 0.03 uM large-nucleus phenotype (e3) from the high-dose collapsed phenotype, and it strongly supported truth. I included e19 in the second conclusion's key_evidence but did not update probabilities to favor DNA damage/replication, retaining Eg5 because high-dose per-well e17 still favored Eg5. In hindsight, ChEMBL lookup returning "mechanisms: none curated" (e21/e22) and name/structure agreement gave no prior to rescue, so atlas needed careful per-dose interpretation. A DNA damage follow-up (gammaH2AX, pH3-Ser10 FACS for polyploidy vs mitotic arrest, DNA content) as suggested in rationale would have been more diagnostic than phalloidin vs tubulin alone, and would distinguish replication stress large nuclei from Aurora/Eg5 polyploidy/mono-polar mitosis.

Lesson: for camptothecin-like agents PMID 16990856, PMID 11034544, biphasic nuclear size with decreasing form factor and modest cell_count loss (rho -0.60 p0.4, e14) plus extreme late actin/tubulin texture should prompt DNA damage/replication hypothesis even when tubulin/mitotic metrics rise.

What was right:
- Detected biphasic nuc_area +28 at 0.03 uM (e3) to -24.4 at 1 uM (e4) with rho -0.80 (e7) and rho -1.00 for form factor (e13) - true for replication stress
- Flagged co-extreme actin (z+69 e2) and tubulin (z+29.5 e4, +23.2 e5) with high frac_mitotic_like rho+1.00 (e8) as ambiguous mitotic vs cytoskeletal
- Review correctly noted pooled atlas e6 Eg5 4/10 vs Actin 3/10 overlapping similarities 0.80-0.88 not clean

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted act_std z+69.0 and act_glcm +33.7 (e2) for Actin disruptors then Eg5 4/10 (e17)
- Pruned DNA damage 0.02 and DNA replication 0.005 at step15 to 0 by step18 despite e3 large nuclei and e11 Aurora-like visual
- Interpreted tub_mean rho+1.00 (e9) and frac_mitotic_like rho+1.00 (e8) as specific for Eg5/Aurora not secondary to DNA damage checkpoint/apoptosis
- Ignored per-well low-dose atlas e19 DNA damage 8/10 / replication 1/10 that directly supported truth after second submit

Proposed next experiment: Per-well low-dose atlas was the informative free experiment; next wet-lab would be gammaH2AX / p-Chk1 plus DNA-content flow and EdU incorporation vs pH3-Ser10 to separate replication stress S/G2 arrest from Eg5 mono-polar mitosis, not actin/tubulin imaging alone.
